# Introduction {-}

Statistics is the science of collecting, organising, presenting, analysing and interpreting data. It allows us to investigate variation, quantify uncertainty and draw well-supported conclusions from available information. Statistics therefore plays a vital role in helping us understand the world and make informed decisions. Governments, organisations, businesses and individuals in a wide range of fields rely on statistical evidence and the work of statisticians.

The *Advanced Higher Statistics* course aims to provide students with a sound foundation in statistical reasoning and methods. This textbook has been designed to provide key facts, examples, and exercises to support students as they progress through the course. It covers the main ideas and methods used in statistical investigations, including:

- Formulating *research questions*.
  
- Collecting data using appropriate *sampling techniques*.

- Exploring data using *descriptive statistics*, such as:
    - Visualising data with charts and graphs.
    - Calculating and interpreting sample statistics.  

- Applying *statistical inference* to evaluate claims about population parameters, including:
    - An introduction to \textit{probability theory}, which underpins statistical inference.  
    - Performing hypothesis tests.  
    - Constructing confidence intervals.  
    
- *Interpreting* results in context and *communicating* findings.

By the end of the course, students should have the knowledge and confidence to plan and carry out independent statistical investigations, analyse data, and interpret and communicate their findings.

## Motivation and Structure {-}

This book is primarily a *course textbook*, with a focus on providing clear explanations, carefully selected worked examples and a comprehensive range of exercises for students studying the Advanced Higher Statistics course. 

One motivation for writing this textbook was to minimise the time spent copying detailed notes in class, freeing up more time to explore and investigate ideas and develop a deeper understanding of the concepts introduced. The textbook is not intended to replace the practical activities, investigation, discussion and use of real data that help students develop a deeper understanding of statistics. Teachers are therefore encouraged to supplement it with suitable classroom activities and discussion.

The book is designed to be worked through in sequence, with many chapters building on the knowledge gained from previous chapters. However, with suitable planning, teachers may choose to adapt this sequence. 

Most sections are designed to correspond approximately to one lesson, although the time required will depend on lesson length, the needs of the class and the extent to which the material is supplemented with discussion or practical work. A typical section contains:

- An introduction to the section's content.

- Key facts to remember, often shown in bold or presented within a note box.

- A worked example demonstrating an appropriate level of detail.

- A selection of questions designed to develop and test understanding, with increasing levels of challenge.

Each chapter concludes with a review exercise, containing questions written in a style similar to that used in examinations. These may be useful to set as homework, and suggested marking schemes can be found on the textbook's website.

Throughout the textbook, the term ‘Data Booklet’ refers to the *Advanced Higher Statistics Statistical Formulae and Tables* booklet available from the Advanced Higher Statistics course page on the Qualifications Scotland website.

## Useful Links {-}

The textbook's website, [**advancedhigherstatistics.github.io**](https://advancedhigherstatistics.github.io), contains fully worked solutions to all the exercises, additional proofs, examples, revision material and a selection of practical activities. Any known errors and corrections will also be listed there. Details of how to report a suspected error are also provided on the website.

The following websites provide useful additional resources:

- [Advanced Higher Statistics course information (Qualifications Scotland): www.qualifications.gov.scot](https://www.qualifications.gov.scot).

- [An extensive collection of AH Statistics resources: statistics.nhost.uk](https://statistics.nhost.uk).

- [Dynamic Maths Exam Question Bank: www.dynamicmaths.co.uk](https://www.dynamicmaths.co.uk/QuestionBank/index.php?levelQ=17).

These links were active at the time of publication. Any updates or replacement links will be listed on the textbook’s website.
